sentences.text:
The Chief Justice
 Justice M.S. Raman
 Order

It appears that although the land in question belonging to the Petitioner was occupied by the State for the purposes of constructing a medical facility and such medical facility is also right now functional, from the letter written to the Land Acquisition Officer, Bolangir by the Chief District Medical Officer, Bolangir on 12th December, 2007 it is seen that even as of that date no steps had been taken to initiate proceedings under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (LAA).

That letter encloses a request urging the authorities "to invoke the emergency provision of the LA Act envisaged under Section 17 (4) of the Act".
2.

From para 10 of the counter affidavit filed in the present petition, it is seen that the representations made by the Petitioner seeking compensation were simply referred to the Government and even as of the date of the reply i.e., 18th May, 2017, instructions were awaited.
3.
The long and short of the above narration is that the Government continues to occupy private land without paying any compensation for well over 50 years now.
There appears to be no legal justification for not invoking the processes of the law to formally acquire the land and pay compensation to the land owners.

4. The Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department is directed to file an affidavit indicating the time frame within which the process of the acquisition of land and payment of compensation in Bharat Kumar Behera vs State Of Odisha And Others ....
